---
# Copy to courses/<slug>/week-WW/seminar-NN.qmd (NN = seminar number = the
# number of its unit and lecture; WW = the syllabus week of its unit). A
# practice session of a practice week: practice-NN.qmd with `practice: N`
# instead of `seminar: N`.
# A SEMINAR HAS NO NEW IDEAS (AUTHORING.md, "What a seminar looks like"): the
# students apply the lecture of the same unit (a practice session: several
# earlier lectures). What it practises comes from schedule.yml (`practises:`);
# a practice session is flexible. The banner shows both.
# A SEMINAR IS SHORT: two short problems (three at most) that together use
# every concept of the lecture(s) it practises. Most students need the
# teacher to explain each problem, so plan about 40 of 60 minutes (60 of 90):
# Recall 5 min + the activity times. No separate Game challenge or case study:
# the unit's mini-game, when it fits, is the tool of an activity.
# The interactive page: Recall, each activity with its steps CHECKED BY THE
# PAGE (2–4 interactive checks: ::: {.choice}, {.order}, {.sort} or {.fill},
# every option or card with its "Why:"; never a closed ::: {.check}) and ONE
# Try it of 2–3 questions (every question with a "Why:"), an optional "At
# home" Task with AI, and a Wrap-up. No glossary: reuse the lectures' words.
# The worksheet (seminar-NN-book.qmd) keeps the same activity with its
# {.check} (results at the end). A personal product (your phone, your idea):
# the page gives fixed example values and checks them.
#   60 min: 2–3 activities, 6–12 questions.  90 min: 2–3 activities, 8–15 questions.
title: "The syllabus seminar title"
description: "Seminar · One short line: what students do today."
seminar: 1
ilos: [A1]
format: lesson-html
---

No new ideas today: two short problems on what you learned in the lecture.
Do each one alone. Tap, sort or type your answer at every step: the page
checks it at once and tells you why.

## Recall

- One key idea from the lecture this seminar practises, in one sentence.
- A second key idea.
- A third key idea.

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 1 · Recall"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="wrong answer"}
A recall question on the first idea.
:   its answer

    Why: one sentence, in the words of the lecture.

A recall question on a second idea.
:   its answer

    Why: one sentence.
:::
:::

## Activity 1 · Short title

The game (or workplace) situation, in two or three short sentences, with
fixed numbers. It uses two or more concepts of the lecture.

![Caption.](images/name.png){width=80%}

::: {.callout-note title="Activity 1 · Short title · 15 min"}
1. A numbered step for each student alone.
2. A second step (two to four steps in all).

*Your product:* one small product: a filled table, a sketch, a decision with
a reason, a file.

::: {.sort}
Step 1: the result of the first step, as cards to sort.

First group
:   a card

    Why: one sentence.

Second group
:   another card

    Why: one sentence.

:   a third card

    Why: one sentence.
:::

::: {.choice}
Step 2: the question about the result of the second step?

- [x] the right result

  Why: one sentence: why it is right.

- [ ] a tempting wrong result

  Why: one sentence: why it is wrong.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 2 · Short title"}
One instruction.

::: {.match extra="wrong answer"}
A question that uses the activity.
:   its answer

    Why: one sentence.
:::
:::

## Activity 2 · A different problem

The concepts of the lecture that Activity 1 did not use.

…

## Wrap-up {.summary}

- What you can now do, in one sentence (2–3 lines in all).
